sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 1m
facts: Official composite DTM provides approximately 99% coverage of England at 1 m resolution
Surface objects are removed to represent bare-earth terrain
The service metadata identifies EPSG:27700 and ±15 cm RMSE
WCS, WMS and WMTS access contracts are exposed
sources.limit: Composite survey dates vary by location; published RMSE is not a parcel-specific confidence interval

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 2m
facts: Official 2 m bare-earth composite terrain model
Native horizontal reference remains EPSG:27700
Published vertical accuracy is ±15 cm RMSE
Used here to test the resolution sensitivity of the pinned 1 m result
sources.limit: The 2 m layer is a QA crosscheck and cannot replace the primary 1 m metric

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 10m
facts: Official 10 m composite DTM is available
It is a bare-earth terrain layer in the National Grid reference family
It is resampled from the lower-resolution composite lineage
It provides an additional coarse scale sanity contract
sources.limit: Ten-metre resolution is too coarse for primary sub-metre parcel measurement

sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
facts: Archive contains site-specific terrain surveys at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m resolutions
GeoTIFF rasters are supplied in 5 km zip files
Heights are in metres relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid
Metadata records survey date, transformation and geoidal model
sources.limit: Historical tiles require explicit date, transformation and geoid checks before comparison

sources.name: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
facts: DSM includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and terrain
It is supplied in the same OS Grid and Newlyn height family
Published vertical accuracy is ±15 cm RMSE
The metadata records date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model
sources.limit: DSM values must not be substituted for the bare-earth DTM height-difference metric

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset
facts: Dataset contains indicative locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales
Files are divided by local authority
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID
A title can contain multiple polygons with separate INSPIRE IDs
sources.limit: INSPIRE polygons are indicative and are not legal title plans

sources.name: INSPIRE current monthly download
facts: Current package was published 5 July 2026
New files are published on the first Sunday of every month
Downloads are organised by local authority
Downloading accepts Open Government Licence conditions
sources.limit: Freshness must be revalidated after the next monthly publication

sources.name: Technical guidance for GML files
facts: Source polygons are captured against British National Grid
Native coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700
Web-map use requires reprojection
BNG-to-WGS84 conversion may shift some features by up to 15 m
sources.limit: Exact containment and raster sampling must remain in native British National Grid

sources.name: Use Land and Property Data catalogue
facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons are listed as free of charge
Licence type is Open Government Licence
Update cadence is monthly
GML is the published file format and no API is listed
sources.limit: Catalogue metadata does not prove the bytes of a particular authority file

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 documentation
facts: OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset for Great Britain
The product is updated annually in July
Grid data has regular 50 m post spacing
Data is supplied as 10 km by 10 km National Grid tiles
sources.limit: Landscape-scale resolution cannot validate a sub-metre parcel span

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 overview
facts: Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution digital terrain model
Buildings and trees are removed from the ground surface
The grid is intended for landscape visualisation and analysis over large areas
Published grid accuracy is 4 m RMSE
sources.limit: Four-metre RMSE supports gross-outlier screening only

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 technical specification
facts: Grid and contour forms are produced from the same source data
Both are supplied as 10 km by 10 km tiles
Grid formats include ASCII and GML 3.2.1
Compressed folders contain data and supporting files
sources.limit: Specification text does not prove integrity of a particular downloaded archive

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data specification
facts: ASCII tiles contain 200 rows by 200 columns
Each pixel is 50 m by 50 m
Height values are calculated from pixel centres
Heights are supplied to the nearest 0.1 m
sources.limit: Current archive headers and raster bytes still require direct verification

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 metadata specification
facts: Per-tile XML metadata follows GEMINI conventions
Metadata identifies the product and spatial representation
Metadata records the 10 km tile reference
Metadata is provided for national products and per-tile supplies
sources.limit: Metadata cannot replace hashes of the archive and raster payload

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 source data
facts: Source terrain is captured as a triangulated irregular network
Mass points and breaklines retain significant terrain features
Grid and contour forms are interpolated from the source TIN
The representation is generalised for small-scale use
sources.limit: Interpolation and generalisation reinforce the coarse crosscheck-only role

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 product supply
facts: Online download is available without registration
The national tiled set contains 2,858 ten-kilometre tiles
Tiles are arranged into 55 one-hundred-kilometre folders
Annual full-tile resupply occurs each July
sources.limit: Availability does not prove that the required TQ archive bytes were obtained in this runtime

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 GML feature types
facts: GML geometries express the CRS as urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700
Spot-height property values are heights above Newlyn or another applicable British height datum
Feature and geometry identifiers are unique within a release
Sequential identifiers can be regenerated after whole-tile refresh
sources.limit: Release-specific identifiers are not stable evidence across refreshed tiles

sources.name: WCS 2.0.1 standard and executable test suite
facts: The test model checks GetCapabilities and DescribeCoverage access
GetCoverage KVP behaviour is tested
Mandatory requirements and referenced XML schemas are validated
Core, scaling, interpolation and range-subsetting classes are treated separately
sources.limit: The generic suite is not evidence that the Environment Agency endpoint was certified by it
